D1 は「すべての解決経路」を完全修飾パス化し、「列挙済み」の compiler-internal trait だけを fallback とする、と無限定な実装範囲・集合を約束していますが、その列挙の権威、保守方法、または保守可能性への解決（既存権威への委譲／保守的 over-approximation／深さ見積り付き strict 実装）が本文にも Consequences にも記録されていません。開集合のままでは実装範囲と fallback 集合が収束しません。

D1 は catalogue-lint に対し、任意にネストし得る「有効な型式」から catalogue identity を「正確に抽出」し、Consequences でも identity 解決を「完全に扱う」と約束しています。しかし、lint 側について既存 authority への委譲、保守的 over-approximation、または深さ見積りを伴う strict implementation のいずれを採るかが記録されていません。Chain ③ に対する syn / rustdoc paths の指定は lint 側の開集合義務を解決しないため、実装深度が未確定です。D1 に採用する resolution を記録してください。これは選択肢の裁定を伴う新しい決定が必要です。

D1 は「検査対象の型式に含まれるすべての catalogue identity」を解決し、未解決部分を一切残さないという完全追跡の open-set 義務を課していますが、抽出・解決方法を scope 外としており、既存 authority への委譲、保守的 over-approximation、または深さ見積り付き strict 実装のいずれかを記録していません。このままでは Rust 型式の構文・入れ子をどこまで網羅するかが未確定です。

This still hard-fails CI on consumer-owned profile choices. `AgentProfiles::resolve_execution` explicitly permits the Fast tier to fall back to the Final model when `fast_model` is omitted, so a valid customization using the same model for both tiers fails `assert_ne!`; the capability-presence assertions likewise enforce the committed consumer configuration. Remove this committed-profile conformance test or move the tier-resolution checks to the existing self-contained fixture test.

`CatalogueDocument::new` still accepts raw `u32` and performs the wrapping internally, while the domain type contract declares `schema_version: CatalogueSchemaVersion`. This leaves the aggregate construction API primitive-based and structurally mismatched; make the constructor accept `CatalogueSchemaVersion` and wrap only at the numeric infrastructure boundary.

`CatalogueEntryKey` only rejects empty text, so `trait_ref_scope` now classifies malformed workspace paths such as `domain::bad-name` as `Workspace` instead of fail-closed `External` (the previous `CrateName`/`TraitName` validation rejected invalid segments). Validate each path segment before constructing the workspace key.

With fully qualified catalogue keys enabled, a valid type-alias key such as `domain::models::Order` reaches this code and `TypeName::new` rejects it, causing the entire catalogue lint to return `InvalidRuleConfig` before checking alias generics. The alias diagnostic should preserve the qualified key or derive a validated display name without rejecting the catalogue entry.

The new public fallible identity conversions do not test their documented malformed-segment behavior. `from_catalogue_entry_key` has only success cases, while `from_fully_qualified_key` tests only a bare key; invalid terminal/intermediate paths such as `domain::bad-name` or `domain::::Port` are uncovered. Add error-case tests asserting fail-closed `IdentifierError` results.

Repository inspection is blocked: repeated direct shell reads fail before execution because the sandbox cannot open `/tmp/codex-bwrap-synthetic-mount-targets-1000/lock` on the read-only filesystem. The current severity policy, briefing, files, and diff therefore could not be re-read, so a valid review verdict cannot be produced.

A fully qualified reference that misses the exact-key lookup falls through to the legacy short-name resolver. For example, if short-key `Shared` exists, `domain::wrong::Shared` can resolve as that entry, allowing `ReferencedRoleConstraint` to pass an unresolved or wrong-module reference instead of failing closed as AC-04/CO-01 require.

`explicit_catalogue_entry_key` examines only the outer type before `<`. Thus `Vec<domain::alpha::Shared>` returns no explicit key, and the legacy resolver cannot find a collision-resolving full entry key such as `domain::alpha::Shared`. Valid fully qualified references inside generic TypeRefs are consequently reported as role violations.

The uniqueness rule now keys on raw TypeRef spelling rather than resolved identity. Because T004 intentionally preserves loose TypeRef notation, two aggregates can name the same exclusive member as `Entity` and `domain::alpha::Entity` and evade `FieldElementUniqueAcrossEntries`. Both forms must be canonicalized before comparison.

`NoExternalReferenceInMethods` searches method signatures using the complete spelling of the exclusive-member reference. A member declared as `domain::alpha::Entity` is therefore not detected when an external method uses the valid unique short form `Entity`; the aggregate-boundary violation silently passes. Declaration and signature references must be resolved to canonical identities, with ambiguous or unresolved names failing closed.

Qualified resolution only searches catalogue keys that already contain `::` and never combines a normal short key with its entry `module_path`. A valid reference such as `domain::alpha::Shared` therefore cannot resolve an otherwise unique short-key declaration `Shared` in module `alpha`, causing `ReferencedRoleConstraint` to reject it and the identity rules to use a different spelling instead of the canonical identity required by AC-02/AC-07.

`bare_name_in_type_ref` performs a boundary-delimited substring match, so a key `domain::alpha::Shared` is also considered resolved inside `wrong::domain::alpha::Shared`. The latter is a different qualified path, but the linter attributes it to `domain::alpha::Shared` and can incorrectly pass a role constraint instead of failing closed.

When the new resolver rejects an ambiguous bare name, `resolve_type_role` retries the legacy short-name resolver. With entries `Shared` and `domain::beta::Shared`, bare `Shared` has two candidates, yet the fallback selects the exact short-key entry and may pass `ReferencedRoleConstraint`; AC-03 requires this ambiguity to fail closed without short-name fallback.

On resolution failure, `catalogue_identity_key_for_rule` wraps the raw non-empty TypeRef as a `CatalogueEntryKey`; that constructor only checks non-emptiness, so ambiguous or nonexistent references never produce the advertised error. `FieldElementUniqueAcrossEntries` and `NoExternalReferenceInMethods` consequently operate on invented identities—for example, `Entity` and `domain::alpha::Entity` can still bypass canonical comparison when the declaration uses the default short key.

`NoExternalReferenceInMethods` resolves each complete parameter or return expression to only one key. If a signature contains multiple qualified catalogue types, such as `Result<domain::alpha::Entity, domain::errors::DomainError>`, `qualified_keys_in_type_ref` returns no key and the comparison silently misses the exclusive `Entity` reference. The rule must inspect all canonical identities contained in a signature rather than require the entire TypeRef to denote one entry.

Ambiguity is represented only as `None`, discarding the candidate paths. When two fully qualified `Shared` entries exist and a bare `Shared` reference cannot resolve, the emitted violation merely says that the expected role was not declared; it does not enumerate the candidates as AC-03/CO-03 require, so users cannot identify the ambiguity to correct.

When an explicitly qualified key is absent, resolution falls through to the legacy tail-name lookup. For a short-key entry `Shared` in module `alpha`, `domain::beta::Shared` can therefore resolve as that entry, so `ReferencedRoleConstraint` accepts a wrong or unresolved module path instead of failing closed.

`explicit_catalogue_entry_key` examines only the outer type before `<`. Thus `Vec<domain::alpha::Shared>` does not attempt an exact lookup of the qualified generic argument; the legacy resolver then searches for short key `Shared` and cannot find a collision-resolving key `domain::alpha::Shared`, producing a false role violation.

Bare references still delegate to the legacy role-consensus resolver, which treats multiple non-target entries with the same short name and same role as unambiguous. A bare `SharedEvent` can therefore pass when two catalogues declare different `SharedEvent` identities; AC-03/CO-03 require multiple identity candidates to fail closed regardless of whether their roles happen to match.

The uniqueness rule uses raw TypeRef spelling as its key. Because loose notation remains supported, two aggregates can identify the same exclusive member as `Entity` and `domain::alpha::Entity` and evade `FieldElementUniqueAcrossEntries`. References must be resolved to canonical catalogue identities before comparison.

`NoExternalReferenceInMethods` compares the complete spelling of an exclusive-member reference against method signatures. If the member is declared as `domain::alpha::Entity` and an external method uses the valid unique short form `Entity`, the occurrence is missed and the aggregate-boundary violation passes. Both sides must be resolved to canonical identities, with ambiguous names failing closed.

Ambiguous resolution is collapsed to `None`, and the resulting `ReferencedRoleConstraint` message only reports a role mismatch. It does not enumerate the candidate fully qualified paths as AC-03 requires, leaving users without the information needed to disambiguate the reference.

Once any token in a TypeRef resolves, all unresolved tokens are discarded. For example, `(domain::events::OrderPlaced, domain::events::Missing)` returns only `OrderPlaced`; `ReferencedRoleConstraint` can then pass and the uniqueness rule proceeds without reporting the unresolved fully qualified `Missing` path. AC-04/CO-03 require every unresolved in-crate identity to fail closed.

The `std` alias fallback compares only the first module segment and terminal name, ignoring all intermediate modules. Consequently `std::collections::hash_map::Entry` can resolve to `alloc::collections::btree::map::Entry` when that is the sole candidate, or become spuriously ambiguous when both entry types are present. Qualified identities must not be conflated this way.

After an exact qualified lookup misses, every multi-segment path is retried as a local module path. If `domain` is a known workspace crate but `domain::beta::Event` is absent, the reference can silently resolve to `usecase::domain::beta::Event` when the catalogue crate is `usecase`. This violates the documented exact semantics for crate-qualified paths and AC-04's fail-closed requirement.

Unresolved bare sibling paths are still discarded whenever another token resolves. For example, `(OrderPlaced, MissingEvent)` resolves only `OrderPlaced`, so `ReferencedRoleConstraint` and the aggregate identity rules can pass without reporting the missing type. Bare wrappers may need special treatment, but arbitrary unresolved bare type paths must fail closed under CO-03.

The tightened `std` alias comparison breaks standard re-exports whose rustdoc defining module differs from their public `std` module. In particular, `std::str::FromStr` must resolve to `core::str::traits::FromStr`, but the code requires module `str` to equal `str::traits` and then rejects the known `std` crate path as unresolved. This regresses canonicalization of a supported prelude trait.

Any unresolved path followed by `<` is exempted as a generic wrapper, including explicit qualified identities. Thus `domain::missing::Envelope<OrderPlaced>` ignores the unresolved `domain::missing::Envelope`, returns only the resolved inner `OrderPlaced`, and can pass all three identity-sensitive rules. Qualified generic constructors must still fail closed under AC-04/CO-03; only known external wrappers should be exempted.

Qualified standard-library wrappers are categorically rejected by the wrapper exemption. Consequently `std::vec::Vec<OrderPlaced>` reports unresolved `std::vec::Vec` while the equivalent `Vec<OrderPlaced>` succeeds, even though cross-crate TypeRef notation is unchanged and both spellings are valid. Recognized `std`/`core`/`alloc` wrapper paths should be exempted without also exempting missing workspace-qualified constructors.

The path extractor treats every ASCII identifier as a type path, including Rust syntax markers and lifetime names. Consequently valid references such as `&mut OrderPlaced`, `*const OrderPlaced`, or `&'static OrderPlaced` fail on unresolved `mut`, `const`, or `static` before the declared type is considered. The removed resolver explicitly supported these forms; extraction must be syntax-aware or exclude non-path tokens.

The external-wrapper exemption is a closed hardcoded list, so valid fully qualified generic wrappers outside it regress. For example, `std::cell::Cell<OrderPlaced>` or `std::mem::MaybeUninit<OrderPlaced>` now fails on the wrapper path even though the previous generic resolver reached the inner declared identity and cross-crate TypeRef notation is out of scope for behavioral change.

The handwritten extractor still treats non-type identifiers in valid Rust type syntax as catalogue paths. For example, `unsafe extern "C" fn(OrderPlaced)` fails on `unsafe`/`extern`/`C`, and `[OrderPlaced; CAPACITY]` fails on the const expression `CAPACITY`, instead of resolving `OrderPlaced`. A keyword list cannot distinguish paths from ABI literals, const expressions, and other syntax; extraction must be syntax-aware.

Any generic constructor rooted at `std`, `core`, or `alloc` is accepted as an external wrapper without validating the remaining path. Thus a misspelled fully qualified identity such as `std::vecc::Vec<OrderPlaced>` is ignored and the rule succeeds using only `OrderPlaced`, violating AC-04/CO-03 fail-closed semantics. Standard wrapper paths need authoritative validation rather than root-only classification.

Review remains blocked before adjudication: the filesystem sandbox still cannot start because its synthetic mount-registry lock is on a read-only filesystem. Therefore the required policy, briefing, current diff, and newly scoped files could not be read. Rerun after the sandbox is repaired.

The generic-constructor guard swallows every resolver error, including `AmbiguousIdentifier`. If the catalogue declares `alpha::Page` and `beta::Page`, an extracted `GenericConstructor("Page")` from `Page<OrderPlaced>` is treated as an external wrapper and the linter succeeds using only `OrderPlaced`, instead of reporting both `Page` candidates. Only unresolved external constructors may be ignored; catalogue-universe ambiguity must always fail closed.

Standard re-export matching requires the public module segments to be a literal prefix of the rustdoc definition module. Valid nested re-exports whose module names change cannot resolve: `std::collections::hash_map::Entry` does not match its definition path under `collections::hash::map::Entry` (and similarly for `btree_map` versus `btree::map`). The existing test only rejects the wrong btree candidate and never proves the correct hash candidate resolves, so valid fully qualified standard paths fail canonicalization.

Standard re-export normalization handles `hash_map` and `btree_map` renames but omits the equivalent set namespaces. A valid path such as `std::collections::hash_set::Iter` cannot match its rustdoc definition identity `alloc::collections::hash::set::Iter` (likewise `btree_set` versus `btree::set`), so canonicalization fails for valid fully qualified standard-library paths. Extend the namespace mapping and cover both set re-exports.

`normalize_lookup` rewrites `crate::` but not the parser-preserved `self::` and `super::` prefixes. Consequently, a declared `domain::port::Port` referenced as `self::port::Port` is searched as a literal `domain::self::port::Port` and rejected as unresolved. This causes the migrated identity-sensitive rules to reject valid in-crate TypeRefs; normalize relative prefixes according to the established crate-relative policy or provide module context.

`is_external_generic_root` classifies the original path without removing a leading `::`. For an unresolved constructor such as `::domain::missing::Wrapper<domain::events::Event>`, `split_once` produces an empty root, so the known `domain` crate is misclassified as external and the constructor error is ignored; the nested event can then resolve and let the lint pass. Classify the normalized path so unresolved identities in known catalogue crates remain fail-closed.

`signature_contains_identity` suppresses an unresolved reference whenever its terminal name differs from the exclusive member currently being compared. Thus a method signature containing an explicitly known-catalogue path such as `domain::missing::Customer` can yield `Ok(false)` for an `OrderLine` boundary and let `NoExternalReferenceInMethods` return no violation, contrary to the requirement that unresolved catalogue identities fail closed. Distinguish genuinely external paths from unresolved paths rooted in known catalogue crates before swallowing the error.

`self::` and `super::` are rewritten as crate-root paths, although their meaning depends on the referring item's module. For example, from `domain::orders::detail`, `super::Entity` denotes `domain::orders::Entity`, but this code can resolve `domain::Entity` instead, binding lint/codec checks to the wrong same-named declaration. Without module context, these prefixes must fail closed rather than be normalized like `crate::`.

Standard-library alias matching accepts any definition whose module begins with the requested public namespace. With a universe containing only `alloc::collections::btree::map::Entry`, `std::collections::Entry` is therefore accepted even though that public path does not exist. This violates authoritative-universe/fail-closed resolution; restrict aliases to proven public re-export shapes and add a negative truncated-namespace regression.

The new duplicate-name tests never exercise successful short-name-to-qualified resolution: the uniqueness pair uses wrapped `domain::alpha::Entity` versus the same direct qualified path, and the only short `Entity` is ambiguous because both alpha and beta exist. A regression that compares raw extracted spellings while retaining ambiguity diagnostics would still pass, leaving the required `Entity` versus `domain::alpha::Entity` duplicate and unique short-name external-reference cases unprotected. Add per-rule fixtures with one qualified declaration and short references.

`classify_catalogue_path` returns `Ok(None)` for every `std::`, `core::`, or `alloc::` root before calling `resolve_catalogue_identity`. A catalogue declaration under a local module such as `domain::std::Entity` is therefore treated as external, allowing role, uniqueness, and external-reference rules to miss it. Attempt resolution first and classify as external only when no catalogue identity matches.

`classify_catalogue_path` returns `Ok(None)` for every `std::`, `core::`, or `alloc::` root before calling `resolve_catalogue_identity`. A valid catalogue declaration under a local module such as `domain::std::Entity` is therefore treated as external, allowing role, uniqueness, and external-reference rules to miss it. Attempt resolution first and classify as external only when no catalogue identity matches.

The standard-library re-export mapping is incomplete. Valid paths such as `std::ops::DerefMut`, `std::ops::FnMut`, and `std::ops::Fn` do not match rustdoc definition paths like `core::ops::deref::DerefMut` or `core::ops::function::FnMut`; they fall through to `UnresolvedIdentifier`. This breaks canonical reconciliation for valid TypeRefs. Cover the complete authoritative re-export set, including relevant `core`/`alloc` spellings.

`TypeRefPathExtractorPort` abstracts Rust syntax parsing and inspection limits implemented by an infrastructure parser adapter. This is an infrastructure capability port placed in domain, contrary to the domain port-placement policy. The usecase layer should own this extraction boundary and pass typed occurrences or results into domain classification.

The added `DerefMut`/`Fn` arms do not complete the standard-library re-export mapping. For example, the parser renders bare `VecDeque` as `std::collections::VecDeque`, while rustdoc exposes `alloc::collections::vec_deque::VecDeque`; after consuming `collections`, the remaining `vec_deque` falls through `_ => false`, so valid catalogue TypeRefs still fail with `UnresolvedIdentifier`. `LinkedList` and nested operator definitions such as `Add` have the same problem. Cover every parser-produced standard public spelling or use authoritative alias metadata.

The expanded re-export table still omits parser-produced `std::sync::Mutex` and `std::sync::RwLock`. The current rustdoc universe exposes internal paths such as `std::sync::poison::mutex::Mutex` and `std::sync::poison::rwlock::RwLock` rather than exact public paths, so the remaining `poison::...` suffix falls through `_ => false` and valid TypeRefs become `UnresolvedIdentifier`. Add deterministic public-to-definition mappings without also selecting the separate nonpoison types.

The bare external-path classifier omits supported primitive/prelude spellings including `f32`, `f64`, `Display`, `Hash`, `TryFrom`, `VecDeque`, `Mutex`, and `RwLock`. Because catalogue resolution already runs first, an unresolved occurrence of one of these should be classified as external, but it currently becomes `ClassificationFailed`; for example `Mutex<domain::Entity>` makes the identity-sensitive method lint emit a resolution violation before evaluating the nested catalogue identity. Align this vocabulary with all parser-supported bare external paths.

`LinkedList` is still missing from the supported bare external-path vocabulary even though the parser explicitly canonicalizes it as `std::collections::LinkedList`. With no catalogue declaration named `LinkedList`, an occurrence such as `LinkedList<domain::Entity>` therefore becomes `ClassificationFailed` instead of treating the wrapper as external and resolving the nested catalogue identity. Add it alongside `VecDeque` and cover it in the supported-path regression test.

`trait_ref_matches` は両方の解決が `None` の場合に raw spelling と suffix を比較しており、完全修飾 identity を経由せずに trait impl を認定します。例えば required trait `PartialEq` に対して `evil::PartialEq`（宣言 universe に存在しない外部 path）の impl が一致し、TraitImplRequired を不正に通過できます。unresolved path は fail-closed にし、外部 trait を許可する場合も canonical identity または明示的な許可集合で判定してください。

`TraitImplRequired` は任意の `required_traits: NonEmptyVec<TypeRef>` を受け付ける公開ルールですが、外部 trait の identity universe が `core::cmp::PartialEq` と `core::cmp::Eq` に固定されています。そのため `Debug` など宣言 catalogue 外の正当な外部 trait impl（`core::fmt::Debug` や対応する bare `Debug`）は canonical identity として解決されず、実装が存在しても必ず missing violation になります。外部 identity は固定した equality 2 件ではなく、canonical な外部 universe/configuration を使って解決してください。

`TraitImplRequired` は任意の `TypeRef` を required trait として受け付けますが、外部 identity universe は手書きの標準 trait 一覧に限定されています。この一覧にない正当な外部 trait（例: `core::ops::RangeBounds` や任意の依存 crate の trait）の impl は canonical identity に解決されず、実装が存在しても missing violation になります。宣言側の universe だけでなく、adapter が提供する外部 identity universe をこの判定に渡して共有 resolver で解決してください。

`allowed_external_trait_identities` は trait implementation の raw path を `FullyQualifiedItemPath::from_fully_qualified_key` で直接構築しており、既存の `resolve_catalogue_identity` を経由していません。これにより resolver が扱う `::external_crate::Trait` の先頭 `::` や `crate::Trait` の crate alias を正規化できず、正当な trait impl を `InvalidRuleConfig`／未解決として扱います。外部 identity の収集・照合も shared resolver の path semantics に委譲してください。

外部 trait universe の構築で、`trait_ref` を `normalize_lookup` した後も `FullyQualifiedItemPath::from_fully_qualified_key` に直接変換しており、shared resolver の標準ライブラリ re-export canonicalization を通していません。例えば `std::cmp::PartialEq` の impl では、canonical allowlist の `core::cmp::PartialEq` と `std::cmp::PartialEq` の両方が universe に入り、required の bare `PartialEq` が曖昧として失敗します。`std::cmp::PartialEq` と `core::cmp::PartialEq` を同一 canonical identity に解決してから universe に追加してください。

`catalogue_linter_helpers.rs` の production 部分は `#[cfg(test)]` 開始位置の直前で 713 行あり、domain の 700 行上限を超えています。今回追加された external-trait identity 構築（特に標準 trait path の固定リストと fallback resolver）が超過を発生させているため、production helper を分割するか、既存の domain identity 経路へ集約してください。

標準 external trait の seed universe に `core::ops::RangeBounds` などが含まれていないため、trait implementation と required trait の双方が bare `RangeBounds` で表現されると、両方とも unresolved のまま `TraitImplRequired` が missing violation を返します。完全修飾 path の impl だけでなく、短名 external reference も解決するという briefing の要件に反します。標準 trait universe を完全な canonical universe として供給するか、adapter の identity universe を利用してください。

`resolve_catalogue_entry_reference` がすべての `UnresolvedIdentifier` を `Ok(None)` に変換するため、`crate::missing::Thing` のような未解決の in-catalogue owner を持つ inherent impl が黙って除外されます。その impl の method は primitive／forbidden-role／receiver／external-reference 規則を回避でき、AC-03 の未解決診断も出ません。明示的な外部 self type のみを除外し、未解決の local/catalogue-qualified owner は fail-closed で伝播させる必要があります。

`strip_type_arguments` は最初の `<` または空白で TypeRef を切る ad-hoc Rust 構文解析です。`PartialEq garbage` を `PartialEq` として受理して `TraitImplRequired` を不正に満たす一方、正当な `core :: cmp :: PartialEq` は `core` に切り詰めます。既存の parser-authoritative extractor を経由しないため、未対応／不正構文を fail-closed にする契約と domain で Rust 構文を再実装しない責務分割に違反しています。

`resolve_catalogue_entry_reference` は明示的 external path を `None` にし、`collect_methods_for_type` はそのまま `continue` します。しかし inherent impl の owner は外部型になれません。`external_crate::Thing` のような owner を持つ impl が黙って除外され、その method が primitive／forbidden-role／receiver／external-reference 規則を回避できます。外部 self type のスキップは trait impl のみに限定し、inherent owner の未解決は常に fail-closed にしてください。

`first_path_occurrence` は TypeRef 自体の形ではなく、内部で最初に見つかった path を identity として扱います。実 extractor は `&Required` から `Required`、`&Thing` や `(Thing,)` から `Thing` を返すため、非 path の `trait_ref` を正当な trait として受理したり、参照・tuple への impl を `Thing` 自身の impl として `TraitImplRequired` に数えたりできます。現在の occurrence 型には root shape が無く domain だけでは区別できないため、parser adapter／occurrence contract 側で root path を表現する cross-scope 修正が必要です。

`first_path_occurrence` は extractor に type/lifetime/const parameter context を常に空で渡しており、`TraitImplDeclV2::impl_generics()` を無視しています。そのため `impl<T> ... for T` の `T` が `TypeParameter` ではなく `Path("T")` になり、同名 catalogue type があれば identity として解決されます。generic label を catalogue path にしない exclusive occurrence invariant を保つため、各 trait impl の generic context を抽出時に渡してください。

`first_path_occurrence` still treats the first nested path as the identity of the entire `TypeRef`. The real extractor returns `Required` for `&Required` and `Thing` for `&Thing` or `(Thing,)`, so `TraitImplRequired` can accept a non-path `trait_ref` or count an impl for a reference/tuple as an impl for `Thing` itself. The occurrence model does not expose root type shape, so the parser adapter/occurrence contract must be extended outside this scope to preserve or validate the root path and fail closed for non-path forms.

`strip_type_arguments` reimplements Rust generic syntax in domain after the parser has already accepted the `TypeRef`, and its character-level delimiter tracking is not lexer-aware. For example, valid `Thing<{ b'{' as usize }>` leaves `brace_depth`/`angle_depth` nonzero because the `{` inside the byte literal is counted as syntax, so `TraitImplRequired` fails closed on a valid root path. Raw identifiers such as `r#Thing<T>` are also rejected because the adapter canonicalizes the first path to `Thing` while the manual comparison retains `r#`. Root-shape validation must consume parser-authoritative shape/canonical output instead of reparsing and rewriting the raw TypeRef in domain.

The anchor check accepts any suffix beginning with `<` without verifying that the complete TypeRef remains a path. A parseable bare trait-object form such as `Thing<T> + Send` yields first path `Thing`, passes line 81, and can be counted as an impl for nominal `Thing`; `Required<T> + Send` can likewise satisfy required `Required`. Root shape must remain parser-authoritative rather than treating the entire post-`<` suffix as opaque.

Standalone paths with trailing whitespace are rejected: after consuming `Thing` from `"Thing "`, `raw.is_empty()` is false and the trimmed remainder does not start with `<`. The injected parser accepts this TypeRef, and the previous matching logic accepted the space form, so valid `for_type`/`trait_ref` values now fail with `ClassificationFailed`. Check emptiness after trimming the suffix.

The `rfind('>')` check still does not prove that the suffix is a single generic argument list. A parser-accepted non-path such as `Thing<T> + Other<U>` yields first path `Thing`; because the suffix starts with `<` and its last `>` is at the end, line 86 accepts it and `TraitImplRequired` can count the compound trait-object form as an impl for nominal `Thing`. Root shape must come from parser-authoritative structure rather than delimiter positions in the raw TypeRef.

The balanced suffix scan still rejects parser-valid generic paths because it treats lexical tokens as raw delimiters. `Thing<{ 1 < 2 }>` increments depth for the comparison operator and never closes; `Thing<'static, Other<'static>>` mistakes the first lifetime for a char literal and skips the nested `<`; and raw strings containing quotes/angles (for example `Thing<{ f(r#"a"<"b"#) }>`) are scanned as ordinary strings. Each reaches `ClassificationFailed` even though the injected parser accepted the TypeRef and identified root `Thing`. The suffix scanner must handle these parser-supported forms without interpreting their internal tokens as generic delimiters.

Comments are not skipped by the balanced suffix scanner, so their `<`/`>` characters can manipulate depth and restore the compound-root bypass. For example, parser-valid `Thing<T /* < */> + Other<U /* > */>` keeps depth nonzero across the root-level `+` and returns to zero only at the final `>`, causing the non-path trait-object form to be accepted as nominal `Thing`. Comment contents must not affect delimiter depth.

`char_literal_end` rejects valid hexadecimal character and byte escapes. For `Thing<{ b'\x3c' as usize }>`, it treats only `x` as the escaped character, expects the closing quote immediately afterward, and returns `ClassificationFailed` at the first hex digit even though the injected parser accepted the TypeRef. Handle the complete `\xNN` escape sequence when skipping literals.

`validate_generic_suffix` treats every `>` outside `{([` delimiters as a generic close, including the return arrow in a function-pointer type. For valid `Thing<fn() -> Other>`, the `)` removes the parenthesis delimiter, the arrow’s `>` drops generic depth to zero, and the following `Other` causes `ClassificationFailed`, even though the injected parser accepted the TypeRef and identified root `Thing`. The suffix scan must distinguish `->` from a generic closing token.

`domain::CanonicalTypePath::try_new` accepts an undifferentiated `TypeRef`, so callers can pass either the original expression or a caller-rewritten expression before supplying `generic_params`. The contract therefore does not make rewrite/classification ordering unrepresentable or reserve it to the canonicalization boundary. Use a distinct unclassified/parser-owned input state so only this constructor can perform the transition.

`domain::CanonicalTypePath::as_type_ref` exposes the canonical value as `&TypeRef`; because `TypeRef` has its own equality, ordering, and hashing surface, callers can again compare canonical output directly with arbitrary raw representations.
